source.title: On the direct summand conjecture and its derived variant
source.version: arXiv v2, 11 November 2017, 12 PDF pages; public published metadata/footnotes checked, full publication not collated
readSections: All of §§1–6, all footnotes and references; PDF pages 1–12 read in full
Rendered arXiv pages 1, 9 and 11 inspected for E3, E2 and E1; André published pp. 90–92 rendered for E6–E8
André adjacent direct-summand arXiv v1, all 15 pages; published §2.5 and Appendix A.1–A.4 checked
Scholze Perfectoid spaces: Lemma 6.4 proof, Corollary 6.7, Proposition 6.14 and Theorem 7.9 statements/proofs read; source-closure limits below

summary: Full main-paper reading with a partial proof-level extraction. Routes import existing perfectoid/derived infrastructure, extend the shared pending PerfectoidRamification proposal, and propose regular-ring splitting layers. Eight source findings are recorded, including missing surjectivity in arXiv Proposition 6.2 and five adjacent André slips. Original-input and publication-collation gaps prevent completion.

items.name: Regular Noetherian rings
items.statement: IsRegularRing R means R is Noetherian and every prime localization is a regular local ring; the local class uses equality of the finite spanning rank of the maximal ideal and the Krull dimension.
proofSteps: Use the existing predicates in the main theorem statements; do not silently identify a local instance with the global predicate without proving localization regularity.

api.name: IsRegularLocalRing.iff_finrank_cotangentSpace
api.statement: Use the existing cotangent-space characterization.

api.name: BhattRegular.localize
api.statement: Request the separate regularity-of-localizations theorem before converting a regular local ring to the global class.

unitTests.name: regular.test_1
unitTests.statement: A field has dimension and cotangent dimension zero.

unitTests.name: regular.test_2
unitTests.statement: The dual numbers over a field have dimension zero and cotangent dimension one, so are not regular.

uses.how: Use the existing predicates in the main theorem statements; do not silently identify a local instance with the global predicate without proving localization regularity.

items.name: Faithfully flat module
items.statement: An R-module M is faithfully flat if it is flat and I M is proper for every maximal ideal I of R.
proofSteps: Ordinary faithful flatness is distinguished from the almost Tor and detection conditions in Proposition 5.2.

api.name: Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_rTensor_faithful
api.statement: Flatness together with preservation of nonzero modules under tensor is equivalent to faithful flatness.

api.name: Module.FaithfullyFlat.rTensor_reflects_triviality
api.statement: An ordinary faithfully flat tensor product detects the zero module.

unitTests.name: faithful.test_1
unitTests.statement: R is faithfully flat over itself.

unitTests.name: faithful.test_2
unitTests.statement: Q is flat over Z but kills Z/2 under tensor, hence is not faithfully flat.

uses.how: Ordinary faithful flatness is distinguished from the almost Tor and detection conditions in Proposition 5.2.

items.name: Ordinary adic completion
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, ideal I and R-module M, AdicCompletion I M is the module of compatible elements of M/I^n M. IsAdicComplete includes separatedness and convergence of all I-adic Cauchy sequences.
proofSteps: Use the existing underived limit; derived completion and preservation of flatness are separate theorems.

api.name: AdicCompletion.transitionMap
api.statement: Use the existing quotient transition maps.

api.name: BhattCompletion.limit_comparison
api.statement: Identify the completion with the inverse limit of its quotient diagram; do not identify it with a derived limit without hypotheses.

unitTests.name: completion.test_1
unitTests.statement: Completion at the zero ideal returns M.

unitTests.name: completion.test_2
unitTests.statement: Completion of Z at (p) gives the usual compatible residue sequences.

uses.how: Use the existing underived limit; derived completion and preservation of flatness are separate theorems.

items.name: Ordinary derived category
items.statement: For an abelian category C with a chosen HasDerivedCategory instance, DerivedCategory C is the localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms.
proofSteps: Reuse the triangulated derived category for splitting obstructions; its existence supplies neither derived tensor nor derived inverse limits.

api.name: DerivedCategory.Q
api.statement: Use the existing localization functor on cochain complexes.

api.name: BhattDerived.retraction
api.statement: A retraction of the unit is an actual morphism in D(A), with composite the identity.

unitTests.name: derived-category.test_1
unitTests.statement: A module retraction gives a derived retraction of complexes in degree zero.

unitTests.name: derived-category.test_2
unitTests.statement: Equality of H^0 alone is not the datum of a derived retraction.

uses.how: Reuse the triangulated derived category for splitting obstructions; its existence supplies neither derived tensor nor derived inverse limits.

items.name: Artin–Rees
items.statement: For Noetherian R, finite M, submodule N and ideal I, there is k such that for all n≥k, I^n M∩N=I^(n−k)(I^k M∩N).
proofSteps: Read the actual statement with its finite-module and Noetherian hypotheses.

items.name: Uniform Artin–Rees lifting
items.statement: For Noetherian R, finite M, ideal I and N⊂M, there is k independent of P and the surjection φ:P→N such that every v∈N∩I^(m+k)M lifts through φ to I^m P for every m.
proofSteps: The library quantifies k before P, φ and m. This is an available stronger control lemma, not a claim that 5.3 itself is already formalized.

items.name: Krull intersection for a proper ideal
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring R, finite R-module M and proper ideal I, the intersection of I^n M is zero; in particular the intersection of I^n in R is zero.
proofSteps: Use this to detect a nonzero obstruction before adjoining roots, and to force a proper ideal containing all roots of p to be impossible.

items.name: Chosen compatible roots and their almost ideal
items.statement: Fix a prime p and a nonzerodivisor t in A with specified elements t_n, t_0=t and t_(n+1)^p=t_n. The ideal m_t is generated by all t_n. Almost zero means m_t M=0; the root choices are data.
proofSteps: Use the same chosen root system throughout each transition estimate; the ideals m_t, m_g and m_(tg) are separately named.

api.name: RootSystem.root_zero
api.statement: The zeroth root is t.

api.name: RootSystem.root_pow
api.statement: The p-th power of root n+1 is root n.

api.name: RootSystem.almostIdeal_idempotent
api.statement: Prove m_t²=m_t, and verify the flatness/tensor assumptions for almost mathematics.

api.name: RootSystem.map
api.statement: Transport the entire compatible system along a ring map, with identity and composition laws.

unitTests.name: root-system.test_1
unitTests.statement: The chosen roots of t in the completed perfection of F_p((t)) satisfy the relations.

unitTests.name: root-system.test_2
unitTests.statement: Unrelated roots chosen independently at each level do not supply this structure.

uses.how: Use the same chosen root system throughout each transition estimate; the ideals m_t, m_g and m_(tg) are separately named.

items.name: Almost modules and adjoints
items.statement: For an almost base (V,m) with m²=m and the required flatness of m⊗_V m, form the Serre quotient by m-annihilated modules, almostification, its right adjoint (*) and left adjoint (!); for algebras use the distinct (!!) adjoint.
items.note: Field-base supplier: PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base. General reusable-base scope is in the current P0 stage; its stronger adjoint details remain a request.
proofSteps: The module adjoint and algebra adjoint must not be interchanged in the proof of faithful detection.

api.name: Almostification.zero_iff
api.statement: M becomes zero precisely when mM=0.

api.name: AlmostElements.hom
api.statement: Give the right-adjoint Hom equivalence; for a module N, (N^a)_*=Hom_V(m,N).

api.name: AlmostAlgebra.leftAdjoint_reduction
api.statement: Supply (!!) commuting with the reductions used in 5.2, under its actual hypotheses.

unitTests.name: almost-category.test_1
unitTests.statement: A module killed by m becomes zero.

unitTests.name: almost-category.test_2
unitTests.statement: An almost isomorphism need not be an ordinary isomorphism.

uses.how: The module adjoint and algebra adjoint must not be interchanged in the proof of faithful detection.

items.name: Almost flat and almost faithful maps modulo t
items.statement: An algebra map modulo t is almost flat when its positive Tor groups vanish in the specified almost category, and almost faithfully flat when tensor is also conservative there.
proofSteps: The 5.2 conclusion detecting ordinary A0-modules is stronger than conservativity only on almost modules and is extracted separately.

api.name: AlmostFlat.tor_vanish
api.statement: Translate almost flatness into almost vanishing of positive Tor.

api.name: AlmostFaithfullyFlat.tensor_reflects_zero
api.statement: Reflect zero in the specified almost category.

api.name: AlmostFaithfullyFlat.comp
api.statement: Compose maps with the same explicitly transported almost base.

unitTests.name: almost-flat.test_1
unitTests.statement: The identity is almost faithfully flat.

unitTests.name: almost-flat.test_2
unitTests.statement: The zero algebra over a non-almost-zero base is not almost faithful.

uses.how: The 5.2 conclusion detecting ordinary A0-modules is stronger than conservativity only on almost modules and is extracted separately.

items.name: Bhatt's field-based integral perfectoid algebra
items.statement: Let K be perfectoid and t∈K° a topologically nilpotent unit with compatible p-roots and |t|=|p| in characteristic zero. An integral perfectoid K°-algebra is K°-flat, t-adically complete, satisfies A=A_*, and Frobenius A/t^(1/p)→A/t is an isomorphism.
proofSteps: This is the star-normalized field-based convention of the paper, not every modern general integral perfectoid ring.

api.name: IntegralPerfectoid.invert
api.statement: A[1/t] is a perfectoid K-algebra with power-bounded ring A.

api.name: IntegralPerfectoid.frobenius_quotient
api.statement: Export the indicated Frobenius isomorphism.

api.name: IntegralPerfectoid.almostElements
api.statement: Replacing an almost integral model by its star produces the stated convention.

unitTests.name: integral-perfectoid.test_1
unitTests.statement: K° itself is an example.

unitTests.name: integral-perfectoid.test_2
unitTests.statement: An unnormalized almost integral model must pass through star before claiming A=A_*.

uses.how: This is the star-normalized field-based convention of the paper, not every modern general integral perfectoid ring.

items.name: General integral perfectoid ring
items.statement: Use the integral perfectoid notion of PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra, allowing rings which do not contain the valuation ring of a perfectoid field; keep its comparison to Bhatt's field-based convention explicit.
proofSteps: The ramified construction first produces this broader object. Exact SW-to-BS convention comparison remains G3; this item does not assert an unverified equivalence.

api.name: GeneralPerfectoid.toTate
api.statement: Under the torsion and pseudouniformizer hypotheses used in 5.2, identify the inverted ring as perfectoid.

api.name: GeneralPerfectoid.fieldBaseComparison
api.statement: After adjoining the unit roots and applying star, construct the K°-structure rather than assume it.

unitTests.name: general-perfectoid.test_1
unitTests.statement: A root tower with π^p=pv for a unit v fits the ramified input.

unitTests.name: general-perfectoid.test_2
unitTests.statement: The datum π^p=pv does not by itself specify compatible roots of p.

uses.how: The ramified construction first produces this broader object. Exact SW-to-BS convention comparison remains G3; this item does not assert an unverified equivalence.

items.name: Perfectoid root disc
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A, let A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩ be the t-adic completion of the compatible-root polynomial algebra and Y=Spa(A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩[1/t],A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩).
proofSteps: The universal root T supplies compatible roots of g after shrinking neighborhoods.

api.name: PerfectoidRootDisc.root
api.statement: Export T^(1/p^n) and their power relations.

api.name: PerfectoidRootDisc.lift
api.statement: A bounded compatible-root family gives the continuous evaluation map, uniquely.

api.name: PerfectoidRootDisc.map
api.statement: Base change on coefficients preserves the named roots.

unitTests.name: root-disc.test_1
unitTests.statement: Evaluation at a chosen root system of 0 is defined.

unitTests.name: root-disc.test_2
unitTests.statement: A value for T without compatible roots is insufficient for evaluation.

uses.how: The universal root T supplies compatible roots of g after shrinking neighborhoods.

items.name: Integral rational localization with roots
items.statement: For a rational domain in the tilt given by f_i/g, with f_i,g integral and one f_i a power of the tilted pseudouniformizer, its untilted integral ring is almost the completed root-ratio algebra from Scholze Lemma 6.4.
proofSteps: Retain the domain and invertibility hypotheses; abstract quotient, torsion-free image and star model are related by almost comparison, not equality.

api.name: PerfectoidRational.restrict
api.statement: Nested rational domains give compatible restriction maps.

api.name: PerfectoidRational.rootPresentation
api.statement: Identify the completed root-ratio presentation up to the stated almost isomorphism.

api.name: PerfectoidRational.tilt
api.statement: Tilting identifies this domain with its rational domain in the tilt.

unitTests.name: rational-model.test_1
unitTests.statement: The whole rational domain recovers A up to the integral convention.

unitTests.name: rational-model.test_2
unitTests.statement: Relations with zero divisors are checked by the derived presentation item, not ordinary cancellation.

uses.how: Retain the domain and invertibility hypotheses; abstract quotient, torsion-free image and star model are related by almost comparison, not equality.

items.name: Tilt approximation preserving a rational neighborhood
items.statement: For perfectoid affinoid R, f∈R, c≥0 and ε>0, there is h in the tilt with |f(x)−h♯(x)|≤|ϖ|^(1−ε) max(|f(x)|,|ϖ|^c) for all x. For ε<1 the two maxima agree.
items.note: Supplier: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma. Source Corollary 6.7 and packet proof read; the entire Lemma 6.5 proof was not independently reread.
proofSteps: Apply to T−g so the same small rational neighborhood has an equation with compatible roots; do not use additivity of sharp.

items.name: Shrinking neighborhood algebra B_l
items.statement: For l>0, B_l is O^+ on {|T−g|≤|t|^l} in the perfectoid root disc. Restrictions B_l→B_(l+1) are the direct-system maps.
proofSteps: Use the actual restriction maps to pass from local almost flatness to adjoining roots.

api.name: RootNeighborhood.restrict
api.statement: Restrictions compose and preserve the root coordinate.

api.name: RootNeighborhood.divisibility
api.statement: T−g is divisible by t^l in B_l.

unitTests.name: neighborhood.test_1
unitTests.statement: If g has a root system in A, evaluation T↦g gives a compatible map back to A.

unitTests.name: neighborhood.test_2
unitTests.statement: Shrinking the domain reverses the direction of the ring maps.

uses.how: Use the actual restriction maps to pass from local almost flatness to adjoining roots.

items.name: Completed neighborhood extension
items.statement: Set A∞ to the t-adic completion of colim_l B_l; use its star-normalization when necessary. Then T=g in A∞, giving a specified compatible p-root system of g.
proofSteps: Divisibility of T−g by every t^l and separatedness make T=g. Footnote 6 is essential: integral perfectoidness may initially hold only almost.

api.name: RootExtension.map
api.statement: Construct A→A∞.

api.name: RootExtension.root_pow
api.statement: The image of T^(1/p^n) has p^n-th power g.

api.name: RootExtension.star_comparison
api.statement: Record the almost isomorphism to the normalized integral model.

unitTests.name: root-extension.test_1
unitTests.statement: The image of T−g is zero.

unitTests.name: root-extension.test_2
unitTests.statement: Root adjunction is not the ordinary quotient A⟨T roots⟩/(T−g) without completion and comparison.

uses.how: Divisibility of T−g by every t^l and separatedness make T=g. Footnote 6 is essential: integral perfectoidness may initially hold only almost.

items.name: Almost faithful flatness of each neighborhood
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and each l>0, A/t→B_l/t is almost faithfully flat with respect to m_t.
proofSteps: Approximate T−g by a sharp element; use the completed root-relation presentation.
At root level k reduce modulo t^ε for ε=1/p^(k+1); Frobenius identifies the quotient with a free, faithful polynomial-root algebra modulo T−g.
Pass through filtered colimits and derived completion using the precise DD.1 comparisons; the source's almost category remains m_t.

items.name: Almost faithful flatness after adjoining roots
items.statement: For the extension A→A∞ of 2.2, A/t→A∞/t is almost faithfully flat with respect to m_t.
proofSteps: Pass to the completed filtered colimit with the reduction comparison; normalization does not change the almost assertion.

items.name: Derived completion and Koszul models
items.statement: Import derived completion for a finitely generated ideal, its Koszul model and the bounded-torsion or regularity hypotheses identifying it with a derived inverse limit of ordinary quotients.
proofSteps: Do not replace derived quotients by ordinary quotients over arbitrary non-Noetherian rings.

api.name: DerivedCompletion.adjunction
api.statement: Export the completion reflector and its adjunction.

api.name: DerivedCompletion.koszul
api.statement: Compare with the inverse limit of derived Koszul quotients.

api.name: DerivedCompletion.reduce
api.statement: Reduction and completed filtered colimits commute only under the verified hypotheses.

unitTests.name: derived-completion.test_1
unitTests.statement: The derived quotient by a zero divisor retains its negative homology.

unitTests.name: derived-completion.test_2
unitTests.statement: The bounded-torsion complete flat situation in 5.1 is a positive comparison test.

uses.how: Do not replace derived quotients by ordinary quotients over arbitrary non-Noetherian rings.

items.name: Perfection of a simplicial F_p-algebra is discrete
items.statement: For a simplicial commutative F_p-algebra C, its filtered colimit along Frobenius is discrete and identifies with the perfection of π_0(C).
proofSteps: Needed for discreteness of the perfected derived relation algebra. Exact original statement and proof are an open source-closure task G2.

items.name: Root annihilation of torsion in a perfect ring
items.statement: If R is a perfect F_p-algebra with compatible roots of t and tx=0, then t^(1/p^n)x=0 for every n.
proofSteps: Taking inverse Frobenius gives t^(1/p^n)x^(1/p^n)=0; multiply by x^(1−1/p^n), represented by a nonnegative power of x^(1/p^n).

items.name: Almost discreteness of the derived root presentation
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and f_1,…,f_n,g in its integral tilt, let B be the filtered colimit over r of the Koszul complexes over A[T_i^(1/p∞)] on the relations (g^(1/p^r))♯ T_i^(1/p^r)−(f_i^(1/p^r))♯. Then Kos(B;t) is almost discrete. For an admissible rational presentation, derived t-completion of B is almost its integral rational localization.
proofSteps: Reduce to the characteristic-p tilt, perfect the derived polynomial relation algebra, then use root annihilation of its t-torsion.

Recover the completed comparison from reduction modulo t via DD.1. Split the discreteness and completion clauses in the final blueprint. The source's unqualified rational notation and its admissibility interface still need matching in G2; no extra rational-domain assumption is imposed on the discreteness assertion.

items.name: Functorial almost faithful absolutely integrally closed extension
items.statement: For every integral perfectoid K°-algebra A there is a functorial extension A→B(A), almost faithfully flat modulo t, with every monic polynomial over B(A) admitting a root.
items.note: Existing node PerfectoidQuotients:Q3/andre-flatness-lemma read. Its statement does not explicitly give the functorial choice required here.
proofSteps: Q3 already owns the stronger p-completely faithfully flat existence theorem for general perfectoid rings. Request only the functoriality and exact field-based comparison of this source, not a second AIC construction.

items.name: Almost-pro-zero tower
items.statement: For a tower of A-modules M_n, almost-pro-zero means: for every k≥0 and n≥1 there exists m≥n such that t^(1/p^k) kills the image M_m→M_n. The later index may depend on both k and n.
proofSteps: This quantifier order is the input to all inverse-limit arguments.

api.name: AlmostProZero.iff_torsion_proIso
api.statement: For each k the inclusion of the t^(1/p^k)-torsion tower is a pro-isomorphism.

api.name: AlmostProZero.cofinal
api.statement: A cofinal reindexing preserves this condition.

api.name: AlmostProZero.eventual_transition
api.statement: Export the later index with its annihilation witness.

unitTests.name: pro-zero.test_1
unitTests.statement: A pro-zero tower is almost-pro-zero.

unitTests.name: pro-zero.test_2
unitTests.statement: Example 3.3 shows almost-pro-zero need not be zero in Pro(almost modules).

uses.how: This quantifier order is the input to all inverse-limit arguments.

items.name: Almost-pro-isomorphism of bounded derived towers
items.statement: A map of pro-objects in D^b(A) is an almost-pro-isomorphism if each cohomology tower of a cone is almost-pro-zero, with m_t fixed.
proofSteps: Use functorial representatives/coherent towers for taking cones and Rlim; state the boundedness used for the cohomological argument.

api.name: AlmostProIso.cone
api.statement: Characterize by almost-pro-zero cohomology of the cone, independently of cone choice.

api.name: AlmostProIso.comp
api.statement: Prove closure under composition using the cone triangle and annihilator bookkeeping.

unitTests.name: pro-iso.test_1
unitTests.statement: An isomorphism of towers is an almost-pro-isomorphism.

unitTests.name: pro-iso.test_2
unitTests.statement: A degreewise isomorphism on H^0 alone does not satisfy the definition.

uses.how: Use functorial representatives/coherent towers for taking cones and Rlim; state the boundedness used for the cohomological argument.

items.name: Tower separating two almost notions
items.statement: For a nontrivial root-valued base such as K°, let M_n=A/(t^(1/p^n)) with transition 1↦t^(1/p^n−1/p^(n+1)). These maps are injective, the tower is almost-pro-zero, and its pro-object in almost modules is nonzero.
proofSteps: For fixed k, M_m is killed by t^(1/p^k) once m≥k. For any fixed transition into M_n, a sufficiently small positive root fails to kill its image in the valuation-ring example.

api.name: AlmostProExample.transition
api.statement: Define the transition multiplication and prove compatibility.

api.name: AlmostProExample.transition_injective
api.statement: Use regularity of roots to prove injectivity.

unitTests.name: separating-example.test_1
unitTests.statement: For m≥k the annihilator comparison is 1/p^k≥1/p^m.

unitTests.name: separating-example.test_2
unitTests.statement: Taking A with t invertible makes every quotient zero; the nonzero conclusion needs the nontrivial valuation example, not that degenerate base.

uses.how: For fixed k, M_m is killed by t^(1/p^k) once m≥k. For any fixed transition into M_n, a sufficiently small positive root fails to kill its image in the valuation-ring example.

items.name: Derived inverse limit of an almost-pro-zero tower
items.statement: If M_n is almost-pro-zero, every cohomology group of Rlim_n M_n is almost zero.
proofSteps: For each k replace the tower by its root-torsion subtower through a pro-isomorphism; Rlim is unchanged and its cohomology is killed by that root. Invariance of Rlim under pro-isomorphism is an explicit E2 request.

items.name: Almost-pro-isomorphisms induce almost inverse-limit isomorphisms
items.statement: An almost-pro-isomorphism of the bounded derived towers of 3.2 induces an almost isomorphism on Rlim.
proofSteps: Apply 3.4 to cohomology of the cone, proving the required bounded/convergence passage. The source's short cone argument is not a substitute for that interface.

items.name: A-linear functors preserve almost-pro-zero
items.statement: If F:Mod_A→Mod_A is A-linear and M_n is almost-pro-zero, then F(M_n) is almost-pro-zero.
proofSteps: Factor a sufficiently late transition through M_n[t^(1/p^k)]; A-linearity makes its image under F factor through F(M_n)[t^(1/p^k)]. No exactness assumption on F is needed.

items.name: Rational annular tower
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and g with compatible roots, put A_n=O^+({|t|^n≤|g|}⊂Spa(A[1/t],A)). The transition is A_(n+c)→A_n. Theorem 4.2 first assumes g is an almost nonzerodivisor modulo each t^m.
proofSteps: The restriction direction and almost base must survive the quotient by t^m.

api.name: PerfectoidAnnulus.transition
api.statement: Restriction maps compose.

api.name: PerfectoidAnnulus.root_transition
api.statement: The root u_(n+c)^e of t^(n+c)/g maps to t^(ce)u_n^e.

api.name: PerfectoidAnnulus.base_map
api.statement: The maps A→A_n commute with transitions.

unitTests.name: annular-tower.test_1
unitTests.statement: For g a unit, the rational domains are the whole space.

unitTests.name: annular-tower.test_2
unitTests.statement: The rational comparison has m_t error, whereas the uniform cokernel estimate uses m_g.

uses.how: The restriction direction and almost base must survive the quotient by t^m.

items.name: Pointwise almost-zero kernels
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, for every m≥0 and n≥1, ker(A/t^m→A_n/t^m) is m_t-almost zero.
proofSteps: In the root-relation model, almost regularity of g modulo t^m controls the kernel; transport through the m_t-almost comparison.

items.name: Uniform root annihilation of cokernel transitions
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, working in m_t-almost modules, for every m,k≥0 the transition coker(f_(n+c))→coker(f_n) is annihilated by g^(1/p^k) for all n, where c=p^k m.
proofSteps: Represent monomials by u^e. For e≥p^(−k), the factor t^(ce) vanishes modulo t^m.
For e<p^(−k), multiply by g^(1/p^k) and rewrite it as a base element with exponents g^(p^(−k)−e)t^((n+c)e). The shift c is independent of n.

items.name: Quantitative Riemann extension
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, {A/t^m}_n→{A_n/t^m}_n is an almost-pro-isomorphism for the ideal generated by compatible roots of tg.
proofSteps: Combine the m_t kernel comparison and m_g cokernel estimate after explicit change of almost base.

items.name: Uniform derived tensor version
items.statement: With the hypotheses of 4.2 and fixed m, the same tower comparison remains a uniform almost-pro-isomorphism after derived tensor over A/t^m with any complex; bounds can be chosen uniformly in the tensor factor as in Remark 4.3.
proofSteps: The source asserts uniform kernel and cokernel control on all cohomology. A chain-level annihilation/factorization proof is still required; do not infer derived annihilation merely from zero maps on cohomology. G4 records the exact unfinished task.

items.name: Uniform estimates for Koszul homology
items.statement: For a regular sequence in A/t^m in the setup of 4.2, nonzero-degree Koszul homology of its base change to A_n/t^m forms uniformly almost-pro-zero towers. The underlying comparison applies to any finite Koszul complex, but vanishing of the source homology uses regularity.
proofSteps: Import generic Koszul construction from DD.1; specialize its derived base-change map.

items.name: Riemann extension without regularity of g
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and g with compatible roots, the final almost-pro-isomorphism of 4.2 holds without the almost nonzerodivisor hypothesis on g modulo t^m.
proofSteps: Apply the regular universal case K°⟨T^(1/p∞)⟩ with T, derived base change T↦g, and take H^0. This does not assert the separate pointwise kernel statement for arbitrary g.

items.name: Riemann extension after limits
items.statement: Under the introductory setup, A∞→lim_n A∞⟨p^n/g⟩ is almost an isomorphism with respect to roots of pg, using the reductions and limits over m of 1.6.
proofSteps: Recover completeness by the limit over m and account for derived inverse-limit terms; this is weaker information than the quantitative tower theorem.

items.name: Lifting flatness from one complete reduction
items.statement: For A Noetherian and A→B, if π is a nonzerodivisor on both rings, both are π-adically complete and A/π→B/π is flat, then A→B is flat.
proofSteps: Resolve a finite A-module by finite free modules; compare tensor with Rlim of reductions.
Finite generation bounds π-power torsion, making the extra Tor tower pro-zero. Lift flatness to all π^n reductions, then use left t-exactness of Rlim.

items.name: Lifting faithful flatness from one complete reduction
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses as 5.1, faithful flatness of A/π→B/π implies faithful flatness of A→B.
proofSteps: Every maximal ideal of π-complete A contains π. Its residue field remains nonzero after tensor with B/π; use the existing faithful-flatness criterion.

items.name: Unramified regular local perfectoid cover
items.statement: For an unramified p-torsionfree Noetherian regular local A0 of residue characteristic p, there is a faithfully flat map to a field-based integral perfectoid algebra over the completed Q_p(p^(1/p∞)).
proofSteps: Pass faithfully flatly to a complete ring with algebraically closed residue field; use Cohen presentation W(k)[[x_2,…,x_d]], adjoin compatible roots of parameters and p, and complete.

items.name: Ramified general perfectoid cover

proofSteps: After coefficient extension write A0=W(k)[[x_1,…,x_d]]/(p−f), f∈(x)^2 and p∤f.
Adjoin parameter roots and complete. A root π satisfies π^p=pv for a unit v; establish general perfectoidness by the cited SW criterion.

items.name: Field-based normalization of the ramified cover
items.statement: Adjoin compatible p-power roots of the unit v to A′[1/p], take the completed integral closure A, and normalize by the almost-elements convention. The newly constructed A carries the K°-structure from compatible roots of p.
proofSteps: Almost purity supplies the almost faithful map. The root-containing ring at this point is A, not the original A′.

items.name: Almost Tor vanishing for regular local covers
items.statement: For p-torsionfree Noetherian regular local A0 with residue characteristic p, there exists field-based integral perfectoid A as in 5.2 with Tor_i^A0(M,A) m_p-almost zero for every A0-module M and i>0.
proofSteps: Compose the faithfully flat first cover with the almost flat integral normalization; retain quantification over all M.

items.name: Ordinary-module detection by an almost cover
items.statement: For the same A0→A in 5.2, if M⊗_A0 A is m_p-almost zero then the ordinary A0-module M is zero.
proofSteps: Use the algebra left adjoint (!!), commuting with reductions, to recover a faithfully flat intermediate model.
Reduce a nonzero M to a cyclic submodule and use almost flatness; containing every root of p would put p in all powers of a proper ideal, contrary to Krull intersection.
This ordinary detection conclusion is distinct from faithfulness in the almost category.

items.name: Adic Hom comparison as a pro-isomorphism
items.statement: For Noetherian R, ideal I and finite R-modules M,N, {Hom_R(M,N)/I^n Hom_R(M,N)}→{Hom_R(M,N/I^n N)} is a pro-isomorphism.
proofSteps: Choose a finite presentation of M and compare kernel filtrations using Artin–Rees; distinguish ideal quotients of Hom from pointwise quotients of N.

items.name: Vanishing lim-one for the adic Hom tower
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of 5.3, lim¹_n Hom_R(M,N/I^n N)=0.
proofSteps: The comparison tower has surjective transition maps; transport derived limits through the pro-isomorphism.

items.name: Splitting obstruction
items.statement: For a map A→C in D(A), form its cone Q and the connecting morphism α:Q→A[1]. The unit splits if and only if α=0. For a finite injective ring extension C=B in degree zero, Q is B/A.
proofSteps: The proof works with this morphism itself and its annihilator, not only a cohomology class of H^0(C).

items.name: Reduction to complete mixed-characteristic regular local rings
items.statement: To prove the finite splitting theorem, use localization, faithful flat completion and residue-field extension to reduce the mixed-characteristic branch to a complete regular local ring with perfect residue field and a finite domain extension generically étale after some nonzero pg.
proofSteps: Prove descent of existence of a retraction via the finite obstruction module, the component/domain reductions and existence of a discriminant element. These are named unfinished inputs G5, not automatic changes of hypotheses.

items.name: Detecting a surviving finite splitting obstruction
items.statement: In the complete local finite-extension setup of 5.4, a nonzero splitting obstruction remains nonzero modulo p^m for some m≥3, and after the two almost faithful extensions there is k such that (pg)^(1/p^k) does not annihilate the resulting obstruction.
proofSteps: Use finite Hom and vanishing lim¹ to detect nonzero reduction; choose k with p²g outside the relevant annihilator power; account for the loss of one factor p in almost-flat base change.
The p²g→pg calculation must be expanded at declaration level; retain it as G5 rather than suppressing its bound.

items.name: Almost purity for finite étale perfectoid extensions
items.statement: For a perfectoid K-algebra R and finite étale R-algebra S, S is perfectoid and S° is almost finite étale and uniformly almost finitely generated over R°. Faithfulness is a separate hypothesis when a cover or almost retraction is needed.
proofSteps: Import the accepted partial node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem, preserving its proof gaps.

items.name: Almost splitting of a finite generically étale cover
items.statement: For the finite injective extensions over the rational perfectoid algebras in 5.4, finite étale after inverting p, the unit is almost split with respect to m_p.
proofSteps: Almost purity plus the finite-presentation almost-purity-to-splitting lemma annihilates the extension class. Original Bhatt 2014 Lemma 2.7 and exact finite hypotheses remain G3.

items.name: Annihilation of the finite obstruction on each annulus
items.statement: For fixed m,n in the setup of 5.4, the obstruction after base change to A∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m is m_p-almost zero.
proofSteps: The rational inequality makes g invertible after p is inverted, so the chosen generic étaleness applies.

items.name: Recovering almost vanishing over A∞
items.statement: In the setup of 5.4, annular almost vanishing implies that the obstruction over A∞/p^m is m_(pg)-almost zero.
proofSteps: Apply the A∞-linear Hom functor to the tower; it becomes almost-pro-isomorphic to a constant system. Lemma 3.5 removes the lim¹ obstruction, contradicting detection.

items.name: Direct summand theorem
items.statement: For a finite injective map A0→B0 of Noetherian commutative rings with A0 regular, there exists an A0-linear map B0→A0 whose composite with the unit is the identity.
proofSteps: Combine the mixed-characteristic contradiction with the separately supplied equal-characteristic cases and descent. The retraction is module-linear, not a ring homomorphism.

items.name: Perfect proper coherent cohomology over a regular local base
items.statement: For proper X→Spec(A0) with A0 Noetherian regular local, RΓ(X,O_X) is bounded with finite cohomology, hence perfect over A0. Its derived scalar extension is compared with cohomology of the derived base change; ordinary base change needs a separately verified Tor/flatness hypothesis.
proofSteps: Request proper coherent finiteness, finite cohomological dimension and finite global dimension of a regular local ring. The almost-flat passage to the ordinary scheme in this proof needs G6.
The existing étale proper-base-change target does not prove this coherent assertion.

items.name: Generic multisection reduction
items.statement: Over a characteristic-zero fraction field, a proper surjective scheme has a closed point with finite separable residue extension. Its closure gives a proper dominating scheme which becomes finite étale after inverting a suitable nonzero pg.
proofSteps: Use existence of a closed point, its integral closure in X and shrinking of the quasi-finite proper generically separable map. Splitting for the composite dominating morphism implies splitting for the original unit.

items.name: Integral global functions in the perfectoid proper case
items.statement: For proper surjective Y→Spec(A) in the corrected 6.2 setup, B=H^0(Y,O_Y) is an integral A-algebra; B[1/p] is the finite étale generic algebra, and Y maps naturally to Spec(B).
proofSteps: Non-Noetherian A is permitted here. Verify the proper/global-functions integrality theorem and localization comparison in this generality before importing them; G6.

items.name: Admissible blowup domination of a generic isomorphism
items.statement: In the p-torsionfree perfectoid-base situation after the finite-cover reduction of 6.2, a proper morphism whose generic fiber is an isomorphism is dominated after p-adic completion by an admissible blowup of Spf(A).
proofSteps: This is the non-Noetherian formal-model input, not merely invariance of a known blowup's generic fiber. Read and match GR2 hypotheses; current F0 Noetherian scope alone is insufficient.

items.name: Integral generic-fiber factorization
items.statement: The integral locally ringed space (Spa(A[1/p],A),O^+) maps to every admissible blowup of Spf(A); using domination it maps to Y over Spec(A).
proofSteps: Take the induced maps on derived global sections, retaining the integral sheaf.

items.name: Integral almost acyclicity of a perfectoid affinoid
items.statement: For an affinoid perfectoid (R,R^+), O is a sheaf and H^i(Spa(R,R^+),O^+) is almost zero for i>0; in the normalized integral convention H^0 is the stated integral ring.
proofSteps: Supplier PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity includes the rational Čech calculation and the sheaf-cohomology comparison request.

items.name: Almost derived splitting over a perfectoid base
items.statement: Let K be a mixed-characteristic perfectoid field, A an integral perfectoid K°-algebra, and f:Y→Spec(A) proper with f[1/p] finite étale and surjective. Then A→RΓ(Y,O_Y) has a left inverse in the almost derived category for m_p.
proofSteps: Normalize the generic finite étale cover by almost purity and reduce to a generic isomorphism.
The composite A→RΓ(Y,O_Y)→RΓ(Sη,O^+) is an almost isomorphism by acyclicity, so the first arrow is almost split.
The change of base along the almost finite étale cover must be descended with its faithful hypothesis.

items.name: Derived direct summand theorem
items.statement: For any Noetherian regular ring A0 and proper surjective morphism f0:X0→Spec(A0), the unit A0→RΓ(X0,O_X0) admits a left inverse in D(A0).
proofSteps: Replace the finite-module cone argument by the perfect-complex cone, use the generic multisection, then apply 6.2 on each annulus.
Expand the derived Hom/lim¹ and almost base-change analogues, and import the equal-characteristic branches. These remain G5–G6.

For regular Noetherian F_p-algebras use the positive-characteristic direct/derived splinter results cited in the introduction.

routes.title: Perfectoid rings and spaces, Part II: ramification and Riemann extension
routes.reason: Reuse the identically named pending proposal in PAPER-ANDRE-18, not a second Riemann-extension roadmap. It has no registered stages or review at this snapshot, so these items are missing rather than planned. Merge this incremental brief with that proposal during design.
routes.brief: Extend the pending PerfectoidRamification brief from PAPER-ANDRE-18 with Bhatt's quantitative version. Import Perfectoid rings and spaces (PerfectoidSpaces) P0 almost-pro mathematics, P1 integral/tilted conventions, P2 rational root presentations and P3 almost purity; import generic derived completion and Koszul complexes from Derived de Rham cohomology (DerivedDeRhamCohomology) DD.1 and derived tensor/Hom from Enhanced derived sheaves (EnhancedDerivedSheaves). For integral perfectoid A with chosen compatible roots of t and g, first assume g is an almost nonzerodivisor modulo every t^m. For f_n:A/t^m→A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m prove separately the m_t-almost-zero kernel, uniform m_g-almost-zero cokernel with shift c=p^k m independent of n, and the resulting m_(tg)-almost-pro-isomorphism. Construct all transition maps on root monomials. Prove Remark 4.3's derived tensor uniformity with its actual annihilator bounds before using it to remove the regularity assumption in Remark 4.4. Recover the inverse-limit Riemann extension only after the quantitative result, retaining lim-one. Do not infer arbitrary pointwise kernel vanishing from the final theorem without g-regularity. This strengthens the shared André ramification direction; it does not duplicate his completed integral-closure theorem or create a second perfectoidization. The standalone derived-uniformity proof is a mandatory design obligation, not established by this partial extraction.

routes.title: Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching, Part II: regular-ring splitting theorems
routes.reason: The existing parent owns Noetherian, regular-sequence, dimension and complete local algebra, but not either direct-summand theorem. These are new layers in its commutative-algebra direction. Coordinate with PAPER-ANDRE-18-B; PAPER-ANDRE-18 is the different Abhyankar paper.
routes.brief: Build on Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra), importing its complete local coefficient and regular local homological algebra rather than recreating those foundations. The first final theorem is: every finite injective map A0→B0 of Noetherian commutative rings with A0 regular admits an A0-linear retraction. The second is: for every proper surjective f0:X0→Spec(A0) with A0 Noetherian regular, the unit A0→RΓ(X0,O_X0) splits in D(A0). Neither retraction is required to be multiplicative. Import PerfectoidSpaces P0–P3, PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra and Q3, the shared pending PerfectoidRamification quantitative tower theorem, DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1, EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1/E2, and the precise proper-coherent and formal-model suppliers requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations and AdicSpacesPartII R2. Construct the unramified and ramified regular local perfectoid covers separately, prove both positive Tor almost vanishing and detection of ordinary modules, and track the (!!) and star normalization steps. Prove the localization/completion, component, Cohen presentation and discriminant reductions, obstruction detection modulo p^m and its p²g-to-pg annihilator calculation, and almost vanishing on every annulus with its lim-one removal. For the derived theorem prove the perfectness of proper coherent cohomology, generic multisection reduction and corrected Proposition 6.2 with generic finite-étale SURJECTIVITY in mixed characteristic. Do not replace coherent base change by étale proper base change or ordinary base change without Tor control. Read the original equal-characteristic inputs and GR2 non-Noetherian domination theorem before closing the graph. Coordinate ownership of any splinter predicate with PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23's pending birational proposal; these statements can use explicit retractions and need no duplicate singularity vocabulary. Remark 5.5 is a question in this source, not a proved acceptance target.
